item.title: Update: Colombia Suffers Widespread Damage From Magnitude 7.4 Quake
item.description: The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 7:34 a.m. A deadly earthquake hit Colombia on Monday morning, toppling buildings, burying people under rubble and leaving more than 100 dead in the Pacific region and the central Andes. Significant damage was reported in the country’s coffee heartland, the region immediately east of the epicenter.

item.title: Connected Vendor Networks Modernize Insurance Claim Payouts
item.description: That gap between payment approval and claim resolution is spurring the rise of vendor provider networks in insurance. Vendor networks let insurers reuse validated payment instructions instead of rebuilding the same vendor relationships claim by claim. The networks connect carriers with the businesses they pay during a claim, preserve vendor payment preferences and reduce the need for every insurer to establish the same relationships separately.

item.description: The breakthrough came when leaders went beyond the AI-sprinkle and instead adopted AI-native daily practices. HireRoad is an HR software business, owned by my investment firm, with just that challenge. The phrase “AI-native” is thrown around a lot just now.

item.title: The VC Firm That Helped Build Latin America’s Startup Scene Is Crossing Into Silicon Valley
item.description: Monashees , one of Latin America’s oldest and most influential VC firms, believes the next phase of the region’s startup ecosystem requires a permanent Silicon Valley presence. She is a partner at the firm who relocated to Silicon Valley from Mexico City. The firm, which was founded more than two decades ago in São Paulo, last year opened a San Francisco office to connect LatAm’s startup entrepreneurs with the money and AI research coursing through the Bay Area.

item.title: Global insured cat losses reach $42bn in H1 2026, lowest first-half since 2020: Swiss Re
item.description: The Swiss Re Institute has estimated that global insured losses from natural catastrophe events reached US $42 billion in the first half of 2026, marking the lowest first-half total recorded since 2020, and 16% below the 10-year average. In addition, Swiss Re estimated that global economic losses from nat cat events reached $100 billion in the first half of 2026, considerably down from H1 2025’s $152 billion and 10% below the 10-year average. Swiss Re’s data on global insured natural catastrophe losses of $42 billion for H1 2026 compares to broker Aon’s estimate of at least $47 billion, and reinsurance broker Gallagher Re’s estimate of at least $46 billion.

item.title: Progressive renews $2.19bn of CAT XoL reinsurance for Florida, $1.85bn for other states
item.description: US insurer Progressive has renewed its per-occurrence property catastrophe excess-of-loss reinsurance program to provide it with $2.19 billion of limits for first events affecting Florida and $1.85 billion of coverage for first events impacting other states, at the June 1 renewals. At the June 1 reinsurance renewals, Progressive has renewed its property per-occurrence excess of loss (XoL) tower, which with the additional coverage from catastrophe bonds and its Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund (FHCF) participation, now provides $2.19 billion for a first event in Florida and $1.85 billion for a first event outside of Florida, also including the shared limit protection purchased at the start of this year. It’s a similar sized reinsurance tower to the Progressive renewal at the mid-year of 2025 at around $2.2 billion , while this year the company has $400 million of outstanding Bonanza Re catastrophe bond protection as part of its 2026 reinsurance arrangements.

item.title: Specialty MGA hires Simon Woodage to build NA Property Treaty portfolio
item.description: Specialty MGA, the managing general agent within MNK Group, has appointed experienced reinsurance professional Simon Woodage as Senior Underwriter for North American Property Treaty, as it expands its presence in the treaty reinsurance market. Woodage’s appointment will see him take responsibility for developing Specialty MGA’s North American Property Treaty business, with a focus on establishing the portfolio, setting its underwriting approach and building relationships with insurers and brokers across the sector. While modelling remains an important tool, underwriting judgement and strong relationships will continue to be central to our approach.” The appointment forms part of Specialty MGA’s wider development of its treaty reinsurance offering, with Woodage expected to lead the North American Property Treaty operation as the portfolio is established.

item.title: Traditional reinsurers face test of discipline as casualty risk remains hard to price: AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the global credit rating agency, says casualty reinsurance is becoming a growing strategic concern for traditional reinsurers as record levels of capital meet uncertainty over long-term loss trends. In its report, Global Reinsurance at an Inflection Point: Can Discipline Survive the Temptation of Record Capital?, AM Best notes that casualty reinsurance presents a different challenge from property catastrophe business because the market is harder to classify as either hard or soft. For AM Best, one of the key questions for casualty reinsurers is whether recent rate increases are keeping pace with underlying loss costs.

item.title: James River’s net income rises 59% to $4.4m in Q2’26
item.description: James River Group Holdings, Inc., an insurance holding company, has reported net income available to common shareholders of $4.4 million, up 59% from $2.8 million in the same period a year earlier. Frank D’Orazio, Chief Executive Officer of James River, commented, “Our second quarter results reflect progress as we execute against our key priorities. Net investment income decreased slightly to $20.3 million from $20.5 million a year earlier.

item.title: Update: ‘Chronic’ Heat Risk in Europe Draws Warning From Swiss Re
item.description: “Record heat underscores Europe’s chronic heat risk,” the authors of the Swiss Re Institute report said on Tuesday. As Europe comes to grips with its fifth heat wave of the year, the research arm of Swiss Re AG is warning of far-reaching consequences. Though Europe’s wildfire risk “is still considered moderate, the increase in fire activity warrants closer attention,” Swiss Re Institute said.

item.title: Typhoon Season Forecast to Be Among Most Intense Ever for Asia
item.description: The current typhoon season in the Northwest Pacific Ocean is shaping up to be one of the most intense on record as the El Niño system strengthens, according to the latest projection by commercial forecaster Tropical Storm Risk. Read more : Typhoon Season in Northwest Pacific Seen Most Active in a Decade “A strong El Niño event has developed and is forecast to intensify further through the rest of summer and autumn,” Adam Lea, manager at Tropical Storm Risk, wrote in the report, adding that this would have “a strong enhancing effect” on the typhoon season. Asia’s typhoon season typically runs from June to October, though the destructive storms can also form in other months.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Small Cargo Ship in Red Sea Kills Three Crew Members, Sources Say
item.description: A small cargo ship was attacked by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis in the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Tuesday, killing three crew members, said two Yemeni coast guard sources and two military officials in the government. British maritime security company Ambrey said the ship was reportedly targeted and damaged by the Houthis, killing three crew members, while at anchor 3.3 nautical miles northeast of Perim Island, Yemen. After the attack, the crew lost control of the ship and were approached by Yemeni coast guard, they added.

item.title: Marsh McLennan Agency to acquire Accel Holdings
item.description: Marsh McLennan Agency (MMA) has agreed to acquire Accel Holdings, a diversified independent insurance and advisory firm based in Waverly, Iowa. Founded in 1936, Accel provides commercial and personal insurance, employee benefits and agribusiness solutions, alongside wealth management and retirement advisory services. The firm expanded through a 2018 merger with Millhiser Smith Agency, which was founded in 1928.

item.title: Allstate develops Allie platform for agentic AI strategy
item.description: Allstate is developing a proprietary agentic AI platform called Allie as the insurer looks to embed AI more deeply across its operations and customer interactions. CEO Tom Wilson outlined the initiative during Allstate’s second-quarter earnings call, saying the platform is intended to support the company’s broader technology-driven strategy. Allstate has not provided a timeline for Allie’s launch.

item.title: EverQuote takes minority stake in Waniwani
item.description: EverQuote has entered into an exclusive commercial partnership with Waniwani and made a strategic minority investment in the company. EverQuote plans to integrate Waniwani’s technology into its AI solutions for P&C carriers and insurance agents. By developing new products and integrating technologies like Waniwani, we will extend our portfolio of growth solutions for P&C carriers and agents and give our customers the tools they need to stay visible and competitive in this new landscape, not just for today’s digital channels, but for the agentic AI channels that are quickly becoming just as important.” – Jayme Mendal, CEO of EverQuote.

item.title: How AI is Changing Insurance Reconciliation Workflows
item.description: Reconciliation is one of the most critical and time-consuming financial workflows for insurance organizations. The Reconciliation Agent is designed specifically for insurance accounting workflows to help organizations automatically align carrier statements with agency transactions and support revenue, commissions, and payables processes with greater accuracy and efficiency. The next evolution of insurance workflows The Reconciliation Agent demonstrates how AI can enhance complex insurance workflows when it is built with industry-specific needs in mind.

item.title: Trump Wins Permission to Revise BBC Suit to Remove Brand Damage
item.description: Trump’s suit alleged that the clip, which didn’t air in the US, resulted in “massive economic damage to his brand value and significant damage and injury to his future financial prospects, in addition to continuing to harm his reputation as President of the United States of America.” In response, lawyers for the BBC issued sweeping subpoenas to the Trump Organization demanding financial records spanning a period of time from before and after the documentary aired. President Donald Trump won court permission to revise his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corp. A magistrate judge upheld the subpoenas at a hearing in July, even after Trump’s lawyer said he would seek to amend the suit to focus only on alleged damage to Trump’s reputation.

item.title: Climate-driven SCS to reshape how insurers price risk: First Street
item.description: Severe convective storms (hail, damaging wind, and tornadoes) have become the costliest insured peril of the 21st century, reshaping how insurers, investors, and asset owners price risk, new First Street analysis reveals. New research released by First Street, titled Global Severe Convective Storm Risk: Pricing Economic Exposure to a Rising Peril, provides the first globally consistent analysis mapping out where SCS hazards collide with dense populations and economic assets, alongside an analysis of how rapidly this exposure is expanding. Severe convective storms have become one of the fastest-growing sources of physical climate risk.

item.title: Appeals Court Says Lobstermen’s Defamation Suit Raises First Amendment Questions
item.description: One of the appellate judges, Judge Seth Aframe, said during oral arguments on July 27 that it doesn’t strike him as a defamation claim and that he finds the case troubling “from a First Amendment perspective.” “The more you broaden the class of people that fall within this, the more it feels like everybody can sue,” Aframe said. A federal appeals court signaled that it might not allow a lawsuit brought by fishing industry businesses and trade groups against a California aquarium to proceed because of the case’s potential impact on free speech. Circuit Court of Appeals is deciding whether the lawsuit can go forward.

item.title: Appeal Court: Social Media Companies Must Face Thousands of Addiction Lawsuits
item.description: appeals court on Monday allowed thousands of lawsuits to move forward against Meta Platforms, Alphabet’s Google, ByteDance’s TikTok, and other social media companies over claims they designed their products to be addictive to young users. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the companies’ bid to reverse a lower court’s ruling forcing them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits over the claims filed in federal court, concluding that the appeal came too early in the litigation. Filed by states, municipalities, school districts and individuals, the lawsuits allege that social media companies intentionally addicted young users, contributing to surging depression, anxiety and body-image issues and a broader mental health crisis among American youth in recent years.

item.title: US FDA Moves to Increase Oversight of Food Additives
item.description: Food and Drug Administration on Monday took steps to increase oversight of food additives as part of the Trump administration’s “Make America Healthy Again” initiative. The rule is being undertaken to “increase transparency and consumer confidence in the food supply,” acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas said in a call with reporters. The FDA on Monday issued a proposed rule that would require food manufacturers to notify the agency when they deem a food additive to be “Generally Recognized as Safe,” or GRAS, according to HHS.

item.title: Booya es reconocida como la Plataforma de Préstamos Digitales más innovadora para la inclusión financiera en México
item.description: Booya, la plataforma mexicana de préstamos digitales, ha sido galardonada como la Plataforma de Préstamos Digitales Más Innovadora para la Inclusión Financiera en los prestigiosos premios The Global Economics Awards 2026. Lanzada en marzo de 2025, Booya es una plataforma de préstamos 100% digital en México dedicada a abrir las puertas del crédito a los sectores desatendidos del país. Este reconocimiento destaca el enfoque de Booya basado en inteligencia artificial (IA) para el otorgamiento de créditos al consumo, así como su valiosa contribución para expandir el acceso al financiamiento en México.

item.title: Can Reinsurers Maintain Underwriting Discipline or Will ‘Irrational’ Competition Return?
item.description: “The key question is whether reinsurers can maintain underwriting discipline or will irrational competition emerge, leading to another traditional soft market cycle,” said AM Best. However, the resolve to maintain underwriting discipline ultimately faltered for many reinsurers in the face of market competition. If reinsurers can maintain underwriting discipline and pricing integrity despite record levels of capital, there may be a new market paradigm at work, AM Best indicated.

item.title: New AIG CEO Andersen Talks Marketplace ‘Pass-Throughs,’ Opportunity
item.description: “They distinguish among providers that are simply pass-throughs for third-party paper or focused solely on excess coverage from those that offer holistic solutions along with underwriting excellence, client service, and responsive claims handling.” In property, Andersen said, AIG’s diverse global property portfolio is an advantage. Eric Andersen, new CEO of American International Group (AIG), offered an in-depth view of the company during his first earnings call at the helm, referring to opportunities within current marketplace conditions. Andersen said the market is “transition from an extended phase of broad positive pricing into a more selective environment where profitability and growth are increasingly dependent on line-specific dynamics.” The dynamics include an influx of capacity in some spots, from excess & surplus lines carriers, delegated underwriting authority structures, and other sources, he told analysts.

item.title: The Private Equity Revolution in Insurance
item.description: Private equity is systematically acquiring the unregulated, fee-generating operations around insurance carriers, with broad implications. Private equity is finding the seams—the fee-generating, capital-light nodes adjacent to the regulated core—and systematically buying them, then using AI to compress cost inside while the actual risk gets parked elsewhere. Insurance enjoys the protection of a regulatory moat.

item.title: FM acquires FortressFire
item.description: Commercial property insurer FM has acquired FortressFire , a provider of wildfire intelligence combining machine learning with physics-based modeling. FortressFire will operate as an independent, wholly owned division of FM under its existing brand and leadership. “FortressFire shares FM’s core belief in the power of data-driven, location-based risk mitigation and protection measures to help clients better understand and manage wildfire exposure.

item.title: RT Specialty launches workers’ compensation program for staffing firms
item.description: RT Specialty , the wholesale distribution business of Ryan Specialty, has launched a workers’ compensation program for temporary staffing firms. The launch comes less than a month after Great American Insurance Group and CoEfficient Underwriters introduced a workers’ compensation program for temporary staffing firms . It provides access to carrier programs, pricing and specialized underwriting through RT Specialty’s local workers’ compensation brokers.

item.title: Aviva expands financial institutions underwriting across UK regions
item.description: Aviva is expanding its Financial Institutions underwriting capability across the UK, adding four specialist underwriters to its regional network. Aviva said the regional expansion is intended to give brokers faster access to underwriting decisions and technical support as it looks to grow its Financial Institutions business across the UK. Beginning this month, the insurer will provide Financial Institutions underwriting expertise through offices in the Midlands & South, North of England, and Scotland, building on its existing London operation.

item.title: Taylor Farms Recalls Salsa, Guacamole on Salmonella Outbreak, Intensifying Food-Safety Fears
item.description: Taylor Farms is recalling prepared foods containing jalapenos from retailers including Walmart and Whole Foods in several states over potential salmonella contamination, the second major foodborne illness linked to the produce supplier in recent weeks. Taylor Farms on Sunday said it stopped sourcing from a Sinaloa, Mexico farm identified as the potential source of salmonella. The recall adds another layer of worry for consumers, who have been avoiding fresh greens at groceries and restaurants after Taylor recalled iceberg lettuce due to a cyclospora outbreak that is already among the largest foodborne illness events in recent U.S.

item.title: Judge Approves $106M Settlement Over Deadly 2019 New Orleans Hard Rock Hotel Collapse
item.description: A judge approved a $106 million settlement Thursday that ends a yearslong legal battle over the deadly 2019 collapse of a Hard Rock Hotel that was under construction in New Orleans. The combined $106 million settlement was approved by Orleans Parish Civil District Court Judge Kern Reese on Thursday, according to Glago and Court records. The 18-story hotel project partially collapsed in October 2019, killing three people and damaging nearby property.

item.title: What to Know About the Salmonella Outbreak in the U.S.
item.description: Here is what we know about the salmonella outbreak so far: Salmonella is a group of rod-shaped bacteria that can cause salmonellosis, a common foodborne illness. health authorities are currently investigating a multi-state outbreak of Salmonella Javiana infections linked to fresh jalapeño peppers. health officials also investigate a multi-state Cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to lettuce supplied by privately held Taylor Farms, a major food-service producer whose customers include Yum Brands’ Taco Bell.

item.title: Anti-Social Driving Crackdown in London Leads to $10M in Seized Sports Cars
item.description: More than £8million (over $10 Million USD) worth of vehicles, including a Ferrari Monza worth £3.7million, were seized in a crackdown on antisocial driving in central London, according an announcement by the city’s Metropolitan Police. Officers from the Met, supported by Motor Insurers’ Bureau, seized a total of 90 vehicles between Friday, 7 August and Sunday, 9 August in an operation targeting uninsured drivers, anti-social and dangerous driving across Hyde Park, Kensington and Chelsea. The seized vehicles include a Ferrari Monza SP2, which had only been in the UK for a day, for driving without insurance and not in accordance with a license.

item.title: Ayman M. Al-Sayari appointed FSB’s Regional Engagement Chair
item.description: Al-Sayari, Governor of the Saudi Central Bank, has been appointed FSB’s Regional Engagement Chair for a two-year term, starting on 10 August 2026. In his role as Regional Engagement Chair, Ayman M. Al-Sayari will advise the FSB Chair and Plenary on how to best leverage the FSB Regional Consultative Groups (RCGs) in supporting the FSB mandate.

item.title: Sidecar evolution driven by asset-side mechanics and valuation discipline: Kroll
item.description: According to executives at financial and risk advisory firm Kroll, navigating this momentum requires strict asset-liability matching, robust valuation methodologies, and a deep understanding of complex collateral mechanics. As reinsurance sidecars increasingly expand into longer-tailed lines of business, the risk profile of these structures is shifting from traditional underwriting toward asset-side management. Artemis recently spoke to Aaron Read, Managing Director, and Michael Sternbach, Vice President, of Kroll, who discussed what sponsors need to be aware of when entering into sidecar deals, as well as what trends their seeing across the space as sidecars gain more popularity amongst investors.

item.title: White Mountains gets $222m capital return from Ark’s Outrigger Re sidecar
item.description: While White Mountains elected not to invest capital into the Outrigger Re collateralized reinsurance sidecar, which supports its P&C insurance and reinsurance subsidiary Ark, for the 2026 underwriting year, the vehicle continues to serve as a major driver of cash flow, returning substantial capital to the firm throughout 2026 so far. While White Mountains did not invest in the sidecar for the 2026 underwriting year, the firm’s latest quarterly results suggest that Outrigger Re still delivered a lot of capital distributions back to it. In the first six months of 2026, White Mountains received $145 million of distributions from WM Outrigger Re, primarily a return of capital related to its non-renewal for the 2026 underwriting year, followed by another $77 million on July 23rd, 2026.

item.title: Kestrel Group sees $6.7m total revenues in Q2’26
item.description: Kestrel Group, a specialty insurance and reinsurance platform, has announced its financial results for the second quarter of 2026, reporting $6.7 million in total revenues despite seeing a net loss of $8.1 million. For the first half of 2026, Kestrel reported total revenues of $16.9 million, compared to $6.4 million reported for the first half of 2025. In Q2 2026, total fee revenues from the Program Services segment were $3.7 million, a 587.9% increase over Q2 2025, a combination of expanding existing and new client accounts.

item.title: Canopius appoints Greg Kuchinski as US CUO
item.description: Canopius Group, a global specialty and P&C re/insurer, has announced the appointment of Greg Kuchinski as US Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO), effective 9 September 2026. Based in New York, Kuchinski will report to Sam Harrison, CUO at Canopius Group, and incoming Canopius US CEO Nadine Moore. His expertise in portfolio management, underwriting discipline and market-leading execution will be invaluable as we continue to focus on winning in areas where we can differentiate ourselves and create a sustainable competitive advantage in the market.” Lindsay Astor, Chief of Staff and Head of Strategy at Canopius Group, added, “We are delighted to welcome Greg to Canopius.

item.title: Munich Re CEO says P&C demand will continue to rise as market moves towards balance
item.description: Christoph Jurecka, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Munich Re, one of the world’s largest global reinsurance companies, has said he expects demand for property and casualty (P&C) reinsurance to continue growing over the medium to long term, supported by rising levels of uninsured risk, emerging exposures, and the increasing impact of climate change. Last week, the CEO responded to questions about whether recent changes in market conditions had altered the company’s view of the P&C reinsurance sector and what factors could eventually drive a rebalancing between supply and demand. Addressing the outlook for demand, Jurecka said that his opening comments on market development, in its Q2’26 results call, were focused on the longer-term picture rather than short-term fluctuations.
